note: Description taken from Holmgren's 1910 original description of Eutermes Ripperti f. Ehrhardti (in German), including the alate (called Königin in the original, but actually an alate) and the soldier; type localities Rio Grande do Sul and Blumenau, Jaraguá, Santa Catarina, Brazil. The author at the time treated it as a form of E. Rippertii; the name is now Nasutitermes ehrhardti. The original is in German and the BHL scan OCR is only moderate: decimal points are often misread as commas or colons and some measurement digits are blurred; blurred values are not cited. The species was then placed in Eutermes and is now in Nasutitermes.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Holmgren 1910 described it as a form of E. Rippertii (forma Ehrhardti); it is now treated as a separate species. Alate body length 21 mm, body width 6 mm, head length 1.65 mm, antennae 16-segmented; soldier head rusty yellow with a darker nasus tip, antennae 13 or more often 14-segmented.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule pale chestnut-brown, the postclypeus, antennae, labrum and mandible bases straw-yellow, thoracic nota greyish brown; abdominal tergites brown, sternites pale rusty yellow. Cephalic bristles not dense, bristles denser elsewhere. Head broadly oval; compound eyes large and prominent; ocelli rather large, only slightly removed from the compound eyes; frontal marks long and slit-like; head capsule sutures faintly visible; the muscle scars at the transverse band form a weak arc in front of the frontal marks; antennal organ rather distinct; base of the postclypeus rather short. Antennae 16-segmented: segment 3 shorter than segment 2 and equal to segment 4. Pronotum half as long as wide, anterior margin straight, posterior margin concave in the middle. Measurements: body length 21 mm; body width 6 mm; head length 1.65 mm; from the anterior margin of the transverse band to the occiput 1.15 mm (the head width figure is blurred in the OCR and is not cited).

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule rusty yellow, nasus tip darker; body dorsum yellow to rusty yellow to pale brown, venter and legs paler. Head with a few bristles at the base of the nasus and on the vertex; abdominal tergites densely covered with very fine hairs, with longer bristles on the posterior margins; sternite hairs longer than those of the tergites. Frontal outline rather straight, with an elevation at the base of the nasus; the dorsal outline of the nasus forms a straight line with the vertex. Antennae sometimes 13-segmented, usually 14-segmented. Pronotum saddle-shaped. (The soldier measurements are given in the original only as comparisons, with no separate figures, so they are not cited.)
